html:
The Tsimané are an Indigenous people of the forests and rivers of Beni in lowland Bolivia, around the Maniqui River near San Borja. They speak a language closely related to that of the Mosetén.

They live by farming small plots of plantains, rice and manioc, and by fishing, hunting and gathering. Unlike their neighbours in the Moxos missions, they mostly avoided mission life in the colonial period. Since 2002 doctors and anthropologists have studied their health closely; in 2017 a study reported that they had the healthiest arteries of any population yet measured, which researchers linked to their active life and low-fat diet. Their neighbours include the Tacana and Yuracaré.
